chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Entering the 81 Theater amateur show
summary: Aged seven, he is told to enter Saturday's amateur show; his aunt teaches him three songs his mother liked while J. D. stays home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I was about -- I was little. I was only seven years old then. And she says, 'Would you like that? I say, 'Yes, ma'am.' So she says, 'Have you ever worked in a theater before? And I say, 'Why no, ma'am, I haven't.' I say, 'I've been on the radio. I worked for the American Broadcasting Company on Children's Hour.'

She say, 'Well, what you should do is go in the theater there on the amateur show and get in the amateur show and go on stage, said, your mother would like that. It would be a nice surprise for your mother when she come. So I say, 'Yes, ma'am, say, how would I do that?' She say, 'Well, just -- you just come to the theater and come backstage, go to the box office there and tell them at the box office you would like to be one of the amateurs in the amateur show.'

So I say, 'Yes, ma'am, thank you very much.' And sure enough, that's what I did. Then when amateurs' day came, which was Saturday, I was in the show. So that particular Saturday J. D. wasn't in the amateur show at all. He was taking care of his mother. He was eight years old at that time, but he was all she had, you see, and so eventually I saw him. I told him that I was going to go in the amateur show, you know, and I was trying to get my playmates to come to see me, you see, as cheerleaders, you know.
And so I got my Aunt Edna B. Saunders to teach me

the words to a song that I knew my mother liked, which was "Harvest Moon" and "Carolina Moon" and "Darktown Strutter's Ball." So those were the three songs that she taught me the words to, how to say them, sing them, you know. And I went in -- when I went in to the show, the amateur contest, the people liked my singing, and all, you know, and they were saying, more, more, come back, more, dance, dance.
